title: My thoughts on The Invisible Man (2020)

commenti.body: The horror elements of this movie are great, this movie genuinely scared me and my housemate. But the story building scenes were netflix tier. The scene where she is celebrating her black friend’s kid getting into college or something was laughably bad. Felt like a weird hallmark movie.
You just reminded me. I did find it weird she slept in the same bed as the daughter.
[removed]

This movie is seriously underrated IMO. So many of the directing choices are genius, and I also loved Whannell's previous movie, Upgrade, for similar reasons. Really curious about what he's working on next, because it feels like he's one of those guys who teases 10 projects that never get made, the big one right now being an Escape From New York reboot.

Universal’s failed Dark Universe was Tom Cruise’s Mummy and sort-of Dracula Untold. After that, they’ve allowed filmmakers to treat each character separately with their own take. Invisible Man went well. Renfield was a disaster because it slams together the interesting story from the trailer with an awful mob movie that absolutely doesn’t work.
[removed]

Shane gillis has a hilarious and totally accurate breakdown of this movie. I actually enjoyed it when I watched it,although its kind of a dumb fun movie that requires you to shut your brain off.

The ex was living in the attic the whole time? Come on

Also very interesting part I liked about the movie was when the camera angle is from the invisible man's perspective there are scatters of light probably because he is seeing inside from the invisible later or something. Very interesting detail added to the filmmaking to make the experience incredible.

I remember it being the last film I saw in the cinema before lockdown so its been while but from what I remember the first half of the film was genuinely great psychological horror.

The film was ambiguous with wether or not there was an invisible man, it plays on the paranoia/PTSD of the main character as a result of her abusive relationship.

The film creates this unnerving feeling with its use of camera blocking by creating negative space you always feel someone is in the room, it was very well done.

Unfortunately it turns into a comic book film towards the end (*im gonna go ahead and blame universal for this *)by revealing way too much about the villain/monster it loses the horror/ mystery aspect of the premise. 

Somehow the invisibility suit seemingly grants the wearer super human strength and agility, the tonal shift wasn’t too far off that dreadful Hollow Man film (*though nowhere near as bad*) overall decent somewhat underrated film though I do wish it ended as a psychological horror rather than the Marvel/DC film it ended as.
I liked Dracula Untold. I was hoping for a sequel or two but oh, well.
Elizabeth Moss deserved an academy award for this.  She didn't even get nominated.  One of the best performances I've ever seen.  She was acting across from nothing but made it feel incredibly real.
Whannell is a serious talent but this project felt a little underwhelming. Guy can do more.

how are they going to make a renfield movie where majority of the screen time doesn't revolve around Dracula and renfield, but is instead dedicated to the most bland and generic mob/cop corruption story.
It’s a movie made for white women 😂😂😂
Whannell is a better director than James Wan who both started together on Saw.
I agree. She did a wonderful job.
Good point on the suit. I thought it strange, and really unnecessary for it to enhance strength.
It's definitely a turn your brain off type of movie. I really struggled watching the last half.

Good that you point out the title, because it's what makes you understand the point of those shots that linger on seemingly nothing. It's funny that something so basic as the title of the movie influences how you watch it. Probably happens with many others, but this movie is the first that comes to mind when I think this. And it's a super basic title!

Somehow the security cameras in the restaurant don't fill a floating knife killing her sister and she gets arrested??? Man it was the last movie I saw in theaters before COVID started and was so bummed out.

It would have been better served to have been given a different title.

It has nothing to do with the novel or previous Universal films from decades ago.

I will give Universal some props, over their attempt at bringing a good suspense drama to the screen. 
U is trying to resurrect their classic monsters from the 30s-40s and appeal to a new and younger audience. I get it....but you cannot improve on the greatness and legacy of those films, so stop trying.

I thought Dracula: Untold was an interesting take. Evidently I was the only one who enjoyed it....and it left the door open for a sequel, say it now: "Let The Games Begin."

It's like Lifetime TV network got Cronenberg to direct a film.


Which is to say, ridiculous plot holes and questionable 3rd act exposition aside, I loved this film.

Its funny, because I so rarely goto the theater and watch a movie. When I tend to-- I judge it so much harsher... If you watched it via streaming or pirating, I feel you'd have a different veiw, maybe slightly less harsh.  I'm  Not defending the film(it has a ton of valid criticism) but paying for a subpar movie makes me hate it so much more, because the price of ticket and popcorn(a necessity IMO foe the price of admission) almost always isn't worth it..... only reason I enjoyed it was cobid depriving me of solid new content so I considered this "decent, but not worth a rewatch or over thinking.

Last time I enjoyed going out for a movie was OUATIH for me... was reaaaally hoping "nope" would be worth, but was a hard letdown
